results.glossary_rows:
| clock tree | The routing structure sources → muxes → dividers → consumers: a clock's frequency is a path property (selected source ÷ divider), never a stored number. Since 701853d, `_clk_*_freq` walks it via `_clock_source_frequency(source)/div` instead of hardwiring DCO/LFXT. |
| SELM/SELS/SELA | The CSCTL2 source-select mux fields (SLAU367P §3.3.2). SELM/SELS share the six-entry menu {LFXT, VLO, LFMODCLK, DCO, MODCLK, HFXT}; SELA offers only {LFXT, VLO, LFMODCLK}. Mirrored by two frozensets; unencodable tokens (REFO, BANANA) draw SCPI -224. |
| DIVM/DIVS/DIVA | The CSCTL3 clock dividers (SLAU367P §3.3.3): 3-bit fields encoding powers of two /1–/32 only. `VALID_CLOCK_DIVIDERS = {1,2,4,8,16,32}`; /64 has no encoding and is rejected with -222, leaving prior state unchanged. |
| VLO | The internal very-low-power oscillator: ~9.4 kHz typical, uncalibrated, no configuration register (SLAU367P §3.2.6). Modeled as the constant `VLO_FREQUENCY_HZ = 9400.0` — a valid source for all three clocks, ~3.49× slower than LFXT's 32768 Hz. |
| MODCLK | The internal ~4.8-MHz module oscillator (SLAU367P §3.2.5), fixed-rate with no register: `MODCLK_FREQUENCY_HZ = 4.8e6`. A documented MCLK/SMCLK source (SELM encoding 4) that the pre-701853d model wrongly rejected while accepting the nonexistent REFO. |
| LFMODCLK | MODCLK through a fixed, non-configurable /128 → 37.5 kHz (SLAU367P §3.2.5). Coded as the relationship `MODCLK_FREQUENCY_HZ / 128`, not a second literal. The only crystal-free low-frequency ACLK source besides VLO; LFMODCLK/8 reports 4688 (4687.5 rounded by `:.0f`). |
| DCO | The digitally controlled oscillator: tunable (`clock.dco_frequency`, default 1e6) and drift-affected (`_dco_actual()` = setting × `dco_factor()`, ±3.5% CORNER). Reset-default source for MCLK/SMCLK — and the only branch of `_clock_source_frequency()` that carries drift. |
| derived-value query | A query answered by computing from the governing configuration chain at read time (resolve source → base frequency → apply divider), never from a cache or a default. The old `CLOCK:*:FREQUENCY?` always read DCO/LFXT — stored, echoed, never consulted — the bug class 701853d fixed. |

results.glossary_rows:
| PxREN | The MSP430 per-port pull-resistor-enable register (SLAU367P §12.2.4, Table 12-1): one bit per pin connects a weak resistor; the pin's PxOUT bit selects the direction (0=pulldown, 1=pullup). Modeled as the stored `resistor_enable` field, exposed via `GPIO:PORTn:RESISTOR:ENABLE` (`_gpio_ren`). |
| register repurposing | One register bit meaning different things depending on other state — PxOUT is the drive level when PxDIR=1 but the pull-direction select when PxDIR=0 and PxREN=1 (cf. TAxCCRn under the CAP bit). The model must store the documented registers and derive meanings, not one storage per meaning. |
| inexpressible state | A simulator state no register-write sequence can produce on the real part, e.g. both pulls active on one pin under the old independent masks (`probe_gpio_pull_both`). Tests passing there certify nothing; the fix makes it unrepresentable — `pullup & pulldown == 0` by construction. |
| derived view | A value computed at read time from stored registers instead of stored itself: `pullup = REN & OUT & 0xFF`, `pulldown = REN & ~OUT & 0xFF` as read-only `@property`s on `GPIOPort`. Cannot desynchronise from its sources; the `& 0xFF` clamps Python's unbounded `~` to the port's 8 lines. |
| deprecated alias | A kept-for-compatibility command that owns no state and composes the real registers: `GPIO:PORTn:PULLUP m` does `REN \|= m; OUT \|= m`, PULLDOWN does `REN \|= m; OUT &= ~m`; queries return the derived views. Old scripts keep working, impossible states stay impossible. |
| pull-up / pull-down | A weak resistor tying an undriven input pin to VCC (reads 1) or GND (reads 0) so it doesn't float. On MSP430 mutually exclusive per pin: one PxREN enable, one PxOUT direction bit — `RESISTOR:ENABLE 0xFF` + `OUTPUT 0xFF` makes an all-input port read `0xFF`. |
| undriven pin | An input pin nobody drives. With REN clear it reads the injected value (floats on hardware); with REN set, `_gpio_inp` returns PxOUT's bit — the pull level — and masks injection out (`& ~resistor_enable`): no drive-strength model, so simulating an external override means clearing REN first. |
| single source of truth (registers) | Storing exactly the documented registers (`direction`, `output`, `input`, `resistor_enable`) once each and deriving every other representation, so one write updates all views and no two copies can disagree — the same discipline as the PERIOD→TAxCCR0 aliasing fix. |

results.glossary_rows:
| MSP430X / CPUX | TI's extended MSP430 CPU (SLAU367P §4.3): R0–R15 widened to 20 bits and the address space to 1 MB while 16-bit instruction encodings run unchanged. `_cpu_reg` now masks writes with `& 0xFFFFF`; the old `& 0xFFFF` modelled the wrong CPU. |
| 20-bit register | A register with 20 physical flip-flops (max 0xFFFFF = 1,048,575); bits 19:16 select one of sixteen 64-KB pages. `probe_cpu_reg_20bit` pins the round trip: write 0x12345, read back `"0x12345"` — the old 16-bit mask returned `"0x2345"` with no error. |
| address space | The set of addresses a CPU can generate: 2^20 = 1 MB on CPUX (0x00000–0xFFFFF). 208 of the FR5994's 256 KB of FRAM live above 0xFFFF (0x10000–0x43FFF), unreachable by 16-bit pointers — why `CPU:PC` validates 0 ≤ v ≤ 0xFFFFF. |
| word alignment | Words live at even addresses; PC bit 0 is architecturally always 0 (SLAU367P §4.3.1) — an odd PC has no silicon state. `CPU:PC 0x4001` → -222 "PC must be word-aligned"; plain memory stays byte-addressable (`MEMORY:WRITE 0xFFFF,…` is fine). |
| reset vector | The little-endian 16-bit word at 0xFFFE/0xFFFF holding the post-reset entry address — firmware data placed by the linker, not a chip property. `_reset_vector_pc()` assembles `((hi or 0) << 8) \| (lo or 0)`; being 16-bit, reset always lands below 0x10000. |
| PUC-time PC fetch | The end of every BOR→POR→PUC reset chain (SLAU367P §1.2): hardware loads the PC by reading the reset vector. `_cpu_reset` and `*RST` now call `_reset_vector_pc()` (default 0x4000, the FR5994 FRAM code start) instead of the old wrong-part constant 0xC000. |
| write masking width | The bit-width a stored-state model truncates writes to. Masking is the faithful policy for data registers, but the constant asserts which hardware is modelled — 07f1f69's register fix is one digit, `& 0xFFFF` → `& 0xFFFFF`, versus the PC's reject-with--222 policy. |
| binary compatibility | Existing machine code runs unchanged on the newer CPU: on CPUX, 16-bit writes clear register bits 19:16 and 16-bit reads can't observe them, so legacy binaries neither set nor see the extra width — only extended instructions (MOVA/CALLA/.A) opt in. |

results.glossary_rows:
| WDTPW | The watchdog write password: bits 15–8 of every WDTCTL write must be 0x5A (SLAU367P §24.2) or the write is a violation. Checked as `(value >> 8) != WDT_PASSWORD` in `_wdt_password`; not a secret but a statistical guard — deliberate writes always know it, runaway writes hit it 1 time in 256. |
| PUC | Power-up clear — the mildest MSP430 reset (SLAU367P §1.2): PC reloaded from the reset vector, SR (incl. GIE) cleared, peripherals defaulted, watchdog running. Non-POR causes are all software faults (WDT expiry, register password violations, vacant-memory fetch). Modeled as the shared `_do_reset()` path; queues no SCPI error — the reset is the response. |
| BOR/POR/PUC hierarchy | The three nested reset levels: BOR (power-up, supply droop) triggers POR, which triggers PUC — never the reverse. The level carries diagnostics: a WDT event causes only a PUC. Silmulator collapses all three into `_do_reset`, modeling PUC consequences rather than the cause machinery. |
| watchdog (WDT_A) | A hardware countdown that PUCs the device unless firmware services it; wakes from every PUC running (WDTHOLD = 0). Modeled as `WDTState.hold` with two doors into one bit — `WDT:STATE HOLD\|START` and the password-gated `WDT:PASSWORD` write (bit 7, `WDT_HOLD_BIT = 0x80`). No expiry is modeled: time does not pass, so only password violations reset. |
| protection by reset | Answering an invalid write to a safety-critical register with a reset instead of an error flag: runaway code never checks flags, but a reset ends its execution immediately and restores known-good state. `_wdt_password`'s violation branch is `self._do_reset()` then `return ""` — no ScpiError. Contrast the -224/-222 rejection pattern used for configuration registers. |
| NACK | The I2C not-acknowledge: a legitimate bus answer meaning no device responded at the address (UCNACKIFG, SLAU367P §32.3.4), not a protocol error. Modeled via `I2CState.addr_buffers` per-address rx/tx queues — WRITE/TRANSFER return "NACK" for unregistered addresses with zero SCPI errors, replacing the old always-ACK flat buffer. |
| GIE | SR bit 3, the master gate over all maskable interrupts (SLAU367P §4.3.3): set by EINT, cleared by DINT and by every PUC. Stored as `_gie`; `INTERRUPT:VECTOR?` is GIE-gated (0x0000 while clear) but `INTERRUPT:FLAG?` reports pending state ungated — the gate and the IFG latch are separate, as on silicon. |
| interrupt vector priority | The fixed SLASE54D Table 9-4 ordering: each source has a fixed vector word address (reset at 0xFFFE, highest) and table position is precedence. `_pending_interrupt_vector()` walks `_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY` (TB0, TA0, TA1, P1, TA2, P2–P8) and returns the first pending source's address, else 0x0000 — the IV-register idiom for nothing pending. |
